what_it_does: This is a high-speed transceiver chip for data-center networks that moves data between AI accelerators at 200 gigabits per second per lane over optical fiber (pluggable optics). The problem: at this speed, short optical links suffer severe signal loss (14 decibels worse than slow links), and existing solutions compensate by adding digital signal processors (DSPs) that introduce unacceptable latency—harmful for low-latency AI inference. The innovation uses a hybrid approach: an older, proven silicon-germanium (SiGe) technology handles analog equalization (amplifying and cleaning the weak signal) directly without requiring digital processing, while newer 28nm CMOS handles clock recovery and link control. By eliminating the DSP bottleneck, it achieves the power efficiency of retimed solutions while keeping latency near zero.
